requirement_text.REQ-054: Port src/engine/snapshot_writer.zig (348 lines -- R-Co's ISS-601, design artefact src/design/iss601_state_snapshots.md) as Letflow.Engine.SnapshotWriter, plus its instance_state_snapshots migration and Ecto.Schema module (schema-per-tenant per REQ-022, same as every other table this stage adds). THIS REQUIREMENT EXTENDS REQ-053's already-shipped reconstruct path -- it is not a standalone module. REQ-053 builds full-log replay from sequence 1; this requirement adds the snapshot table, the writer, and the replay-source selection that lets that same reconstruct function start from the latest snapshot instead. The deliverable is therefore a modification of REQ-053's function plus new supporting code, and the correctness bar below is that both paths agree. Purpose: reconstruction (REQ-053) replaying the FULL event log from sequence 1 is O(events) and gets slower forever. A periodic snapshot of the InstanceState as a jsonb blob lets reconstruction replay only the events SINCE the latest snapshot. - take_snapshot/N: serialises REQ-044's InstanceState (status, tokens, variables, pending task nodes, error_detail) plus the sequence_number it is current as of, into an instance_state_snapshots row. - maybe_take_snapshot/N: the cadence check -- snapshot every N events, default 1000 per snapshot_writer.zig's DEFAULT_SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL. Called after event appends and on instance completion. - REQ-053's replay-source selection: given a latest snapshot at sequence S, replay only events with sequence_number > S on top of the deserialised snapshot state, versus replaying from 1 when no snapshot exists (reconstruction.zig's determineReplaySourceForSnapshot()). This requirement extends REQ-053's reconstruct path to use snapshots when present -- and the correctness bar is that BOTH paths produce the identical state, since a snapshot that diverges from full replay is worse than no snapshot at all. - This table is NOT the same thing as REQ-027/REQ-033's instance_definition_snapshots (the immutable PD-08 DEFINITION graph bound to an instance at start). These are periodic EXECUTION STATE snapshots, mutable in the sense that new rows accumulate over an instance's life. Say so explicitly in the moduledoc -- the two names are one word apart and confusing them would be a silent data-model error. OPEN QUESTION (flag, do not silently resolve): where the events-since-last-snapshot counter lives. instance_projections.last_event_seq (REQ-023) already tracks the latest sequence per instance, which makes a pure row-based cadence check possible with no in-memory counter at all; R-Co's own SnapshotWriter is a struct holding a pool handle. If REQ-045 resolved to supervised processes, an in-process counter is available but is exactly the kind of state stage-3-instance-engine.md's second Early finding warns is NOT automatically worth a process. Leave the choice to CODE-DESIGNER, citing that finding and REQ-045's resolution.

task.description: Idiom review gate on REQ-054's implementation: git diff main...HEAD on feature/WF02-REQ054-20260819. Check OTP idiom vs crutch, supervision integrity, scope creep, and consistency with docs/migration/decisions/ (particularly Decision 0006 D2, and REQ-045's process-vs-row resolution which the ELIXIR-DEV run cited to resolve the design's open cadence-counter question). Also check the flagged error_detail field gap (InstanceState has no error_detail field though the original requirement text mentioned it) was handled reasonably rather than silently dropped or fabricated.

result.summary: Idiom/supervision/decision-consistency checks all pass cleanly: no gen_statem/process-per-instance question is in play here (SnapshotWriter is a stateless module of plain Repo calls, matching REQ-045's already-shipped process-vs-row resolution the design doc cites); no tenant_id on instance_state_snapshots, consistent with Decision 0006 D2 and every other business table added since; the cadence-counter resolution (pure row-based check via latest_snapshot/2, no in-memory/per-process counter) is a reasonable, well-argued reading of stage-3-instance-engine.md's second Early finding plus REQ-045's resolution, and was correctly surfaced rather than silently defaulted; the error_detail gap is handled honestly (documented as a pre-existing InstanceState.t() representational gap, not fabricated or silently dropped, and matches what CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR/SECURITY-REVIEWER already accepted). reconstruction.ex's arity widening (read_full_log/2->/3, replay/3->/4) is a clean additive change: fold_events/3 and every apply_event/3 clause are byte-for-byte untouched, so INV-ISS-1 (both replay paths agree) can only fail via SnapshotWriter's own serialise/deserialise round-trip, never via two fold implementations drifting -- this is the load-bearing correctness property and it holds. All existing callers of reconstruct_instance/2 (test/letflow/engine/reconstruction_test.exs, 13 call sites) still compile against the unchanged public @spec. FAIL grounds: this is a genuine implementation-scope gap, not an idiom/style nit. The design doc (lib/letflow/design/req054-instance-state-snapshots.md) SS4.2 and SS8 both explicitly state, as this requirement's own in-scope deliverable (not a future requirement, not an open question), that Letflow.Engine gains new call sites into SnapshotWriter.maybe_take_snapshot/4 'at its existing event-append points and at instance completion' -- naming create/2, complete_task/3, and ExecutionError.append_multi/3 by name. None of that wiring exists: grep for maybe_take_snapshot across lib/ and test/ finds zero call sites outside snapshot_writer.ex's own definition, lib/letflow/engine.ex is untouched by this diff (not in artifacts_out, not in git diff --stat), and ELIXIR-DEV's own handoff summary never claims the wiring was done or flags it as a deliberately deferred/open item -- unlike the error_detail and cadence-counter gaps, which were both surfaced explicitly, this one is a silent omission. Practical effect: SnapshotWriter/latest_snapshot/select_replay_source are all correct and will work once fed a snapshot row, but no code path in the running system ever calls take_snapshot, so no instance will ever actually accumulate a snapshot in production -- the requirement's whole stated purpose (bounding reconstruction's O(events) growth) is unmet despite every individual piece being idiomatically sound in isolation. This must be caught before TEST-DESIGNER: absent the wiring, a test suite could exercise maybe_take_snapshot/4 and select_replay_source/2 directly in isolation and appear to give full coverage while never proving the feature actually fires from real engine writes.
issues: lib/letflow/engine.ex has no call sites into Letflow.Engine.SnapshotWriter.maybe_take_snapshot/4, contrary to design doc lib/letflow/design/req054-instance-state-snapshots.md SS4.2/SS8 (in-scope deliverable, not deferred). Wire it in after the event-append points create/2 (~line 211), complete_task/3 (~line 840, both the normal-completion and error paths), ExecutionError.append_multi/3's call sites (engine.ex:1263, engine.ex:1948 via set_instance_error/2), and on instance completion (the :completed/:cancelled transition inside complete_task/3, ~line 1496-1524) -- or, if ELIXIR-DEV judges a subset sufficient/different from the design doc's list, say so explicitly in the next handoff rather than silently shipping partial wiring again.
